en: Yahya ibn Ayyub, Qutaybah, and Ibn Hujr narrated to us, they said: Isma'il—who is Ibn Ja'far—narrated to us, from al-'Ala', from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said: "Charity does not decrease wealth, and Allah does not increase a servant on account of forgiveness except in honor, and no one humbles himself for the sake of Allah except that Allah elevates him."

Yahya ibn Ayyub, Qutaybah, and Ibn Hujr narrated to us, they said: Isma'il—meaning Ibn Ja'far—narrated to us, from al-'Ala', from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "The sin of whatever two who revile one another say falls upon the initiator, as long as the wronged party does not transgress."

Ibn Numayr narrated to us: Humayd ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from al-Sha'bi, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), the like of it.

Muhammad ibn 'Abdillah ibn Numayr narrated to me: Humayd ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Khaythamah, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "The Muslims are like a single person: if his eye aches, his whole body aches; and if his head aches, his whole body aches."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, they said: Waki' narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from al-Sha'bi, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "The believers are like a single person: if his head aches, the rest of the body responds with fever and sleeplessness."
Ishaq al-Hanzali narrated to us: Jarir informed us, from Mutarrif, from al-Sha'bi, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), the like of it.

Muhammad ibn 'Abdillah ibn Numayr narrated to us: my father narrated to us: Zakariyya narrated to us, from al-Sha'bi, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "The example of the believers in their mutual love, mercy, and compassion is like that of a single body: when one limb aches, the rest of the body responds to it with sleeplessness and fever."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Abu 'Amir al-Ash'ari narrated to us, they said: 'Abdullah ibn Idris and Abu Usamah narrated to us; (H) and Muhammad ibn al-'Ala' Abu Kurayb narrated to us: Ibn al-Mubarak, Ibn Idris, and Abu Usamah all narrated to us from Burayd, from Abu Burdah, from Abu Musa, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "A believer to a believer is like a structure, its parts strengthening one another."

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, Ishaq ibn Mansur, and Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to us—Ibn Rafi' said: "narrated to us," and the other two said: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us: Ma'mar informed us, from Ayyub, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from Jabir ibn 'Abdillah, who said: A man from the Emigrants struck a man from the Ansar from behind, so he came to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) asking him for retaliation. The Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Leave it, for it is foul." Ibn Mansur said in his narration: 'Amr said: I heard Jabir.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Zuhayr ibn Harb, Ahmad ibn 'Abdah al-Dabbi, and Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to us—and the wording is Ibn Abi Shaybah's; Ibn 'Abdah said: "informed us," and the others said: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, saying: 'Amr heard Jabir ibn 'Abdillah saying: We were with the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) on an expedition when a man from the Emigrants struck a man from the Ansar from behind. The Ansari said: "O Ansar, help!" and the Emigrant said: "O Emigrants, help!" The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "What is this slogan of the days of ignorance?" They said: "O Messenger of Allah, a man from the Emigrants struck a man from the Ansar from behind." He said: "Leave it, for it is foul." 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy heard that and said: "Have they actually done it? By Allah, if we return to Medina, the more honorable will surely expel the humbler from it!" 'Umar said: "Let me strike the neck of this hypocrite!" He said: "Leave him, lest people say that Muhammad kills his companions."

Ahmad ibn 'Abdillah ibn Yunus narrated to us: Zuhayr narrated to us: Abu al-Zubayr narrated to us, from Jabir, who said: Two young men fought, a youth from the Emigrants and a youth from the Ansar. The Emigrant—or the Emigrants—called out: "O Emigrants, help!" and the Ansari called out: "O Ansar, help!" So the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) came out and said: "What is this slogan of the people of the days of ignorance?" They said: "No, O Messenger of Allah, it is just that two youths fought and one of them struck the other from behind." He said: "Then there is no harm; and let a person support his brother whether he is an oppressor or oppressed: if he is an oppressor, let him stop him, for that is his support for him; and if he is oppressed, let him aid him."

Muhammad ibn 'Abdillah ibn Numayr narrated to us: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us: Burayd ibn Abi Burdah narrated to us, from his father, from Abu Musa, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, gives respite to the oppressor, until when He seizes him, He does not let him escape." Then he recited: {And thus is the seizure of your Lord when He seizes the cities while they are committing wrong. Indeed, His seizure is painful and severe.}

Yahya ibn Ayyub, Qutaybah, and Ibn Hujr narrated to us, they said: Isma'il—meaning Ibn Ja'far—narrated to us, from al-'Ala', from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "You will surely restore the rights to their rightful owners on the Day of Resurrection, to the point that retaliation will be taken for the hornless sheep against the horned sheep."

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id and 'Ali ibn Hujr narrated to us, they said: Isma'il—who is Ibn Ja'far—narrated to us, from al-'Ala', from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Do you know who the bankrupt one is?" They said: "The bankrupt among us is the one who has neither dirham nor goods." So he said: "Indeed, the bankrupt of my Ummah is the one who comes on the Day of Resurrection with prayer, fasting, and zakah, but comes having insulted this one, slandered this one, consumed the wealth of this one, shed the blood of this one, and struck this one. So this one is given from his good deeds, and that one from his good deeds. If his good deeds are exhausted before what is due upon him is settled, their sins are taken and cast upon him, and then he is cast into the Fire."

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Layth narrated to us, from 'Uqayl, from al-Zuhri, from Salim, from his father, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "A Muslim is the brother of a Muslim: he does not wrong him nor does he surrender him. Whoever attends to the need of his brother, Allah will attend to his need; whoever relieves a distress from a Muslim, Allah will relieve from him a distress from among the distresses of the Day of Resurrection; and whoever covers the fault of a Muslim, Allah will cover him on the Day of Resurrection."

Muhammad ibn Hatim narrated to me: Shababah narrated to us: 'Abd al-'Aziz al-Majishun narrated to us, from 'Abdullah ibn Dinar, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Indeed, injustice will be darknesses on the Day of Resurrection."

'Abdullah ibn Maslamah ibn Qa'nab narrated to us: Dawud—meaning Ibn Qays—narrated to us, from 'Ubaydullah ibn Miqsam, from Jabir ibn 'Abdillah, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Beware of injustice, for injustice will be darknesses on the Day of Resurrection; and beware of greed, for greed destroyed those who came before you: it incited them to shed their blood and deem their sacred things lawful."

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, both from 'Abd al-Samad ibn 'Abd al-Warith: Hammam narrated to us: Qatadah narrated to us, from Abu Qilabah, from Abu Asma', from Abu Dharr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said, in what he narrated from his Lord, Blessed and Exalted: "Indeed, I have forbidden injustice for Myself and for My servants, so do not wrong one another." And he pursued the hadith similarly; and the hadith of Abu Idris which we mentioned is more complete than this.

Abu Ishaq said: al-Hasan and al-Husayn, the two sons of Bishr, and Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated this hadith to us; they said: Abu Mushir narrated to us... and they mentioned the hadith in its entirety.
Abu Bakr ibn Ishaq narrated it to me: Abu Mushir narrated to us: Sa'id ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, with this chain of transmission, except that Marwan's hadith was the more complete of the two.

'Abdullah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Bahram al-Darimi narrated to us: Marwan—meaning Ibn Muhammad al-Dimashqi—narrated to us: Sa'id ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, from Rabi'ah ibn Yazid, from Abu Idris al-Khawlani, from Abu Dharr, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), in what he narrated from Allah, Blessed and Exalted, that He said: "O My servants, indeed I have forbidden injustice for Myself and made it forbidden among you, so do not wrong one another. O My servants, all of you are astray except those whom I guide, so seek guidance from Me and I will guide you. O My servants, all of you are hungry except those whom I feed, so seek food from Me and I will feed you. O My servants, all of you are naked except those whom I clothe, so seek clothing from Me and I will clothe you. O My servants, indeed you commit errors by night and by day, and I forgive all sins, so seek forgiveness from Me and I will forgive you. O My servants, indeed you can never reach harming Me so as to harm Me, nor can you ever reach benefiting Me so as to benefit Me. O My servants, if the first of you and the last of you, the humans of you and the jinn of you, were to have hearts as pious as the most pious heart of any single man among you, that would not increase My kingdom in anything. O My servants, if the first of you and the last of you, the humans of you and the jinn of you, were to have hearts as wicked as the most wicked heart of any single man among you, that would not decrease My kingdom in anything. O My servants, if the first of you and the last of you, the humans of you and the jinn of you, were to stand on a single plateau and ask of Me, and I gave every human being his request, that would not diminish what is with Me any more than a needle diminishes when dipped into the sea. O My servants, it is only your deeds which I reckon for you and then recompense you for them; so whoever finds good, let him praise Allah, and whoever finds other than that, let him blame no one but himself." Sa'id said: Whenever Abu Idris al-Khawlani narrated this hadith, he would kneel down upon his knees.

'Ubaydullah ibn 'Umar al-Qawariri narrated to us: Yahya ibn Sa'id and Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, they said: 'Imran Abu Bakr narrated to us: 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Abbas said to me: "Shall I not show you a woman from the people of Paradise?" I said: "Yes, indeed." He said: "This black woman came to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and said: 'I suffer from epileptic seizures and become uncovered, so supplicate to Allah for me.' He said: 'If you wish, be patient and you will have Paradise; and if you wish, I will supplicate to Allah to heal you.' She said: 'I will be patient.' Then she said: 'Indeed, I become uncovered, so supplicate to Allah that I do not become uncovered.' So he supplicated for her."

'Ubaydullah ibn 'Umar al-Qawariri narrated to me: Yazid ibn Zuray' narrated to us: al-Hajjaj al-Sawwaf narrated to us: Abu al-Zubayr narrated to me: Jabir ibn 'Abdillah narrated to us that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) visited Umm al-Sa'ib—or Umm al-Musayyab—and said: "What is the matter with you, O Umm al-Sa'ib—or O Umm al-Musayyab—shivering?" She said: "It is fever, may Allah not bless it!" Thereupon he said: "Do not revile fever, for it removes the sins of the children of Adam just as the bellows removes the dross of iron."

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id and Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah both narrated from Ibn 'Uyaynah—and the wording is Qutaybah's: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Muhaysin, an elder from Quraysh: he heard Muhammad ibn Qays ibn Makhramah narrating from Abu Hurayrah, who said: When there was revealed: {Whoever does a wrong will be recompensed for it}, it hit the Muslims with great severity. The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Follow the middle course and aim for what is right, for in everything with which a Muslim is afflicted there is an expiation, even a calamity that befalls him or a thorn that pricks him." Muslim said: He is 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhaysin from the people of Mecca.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Abu Kurayb narrated to us, they said: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from al-Walid ibn Kathir, from Muhammad ibn 'Amr ibn 'Ata', from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu Sa'id and Abu Hurayrah, that they both heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) say: "No fatigue, illness, anxiety, sorrow, harm, or distress afflicts a believer, even the worry that troubles him, but that Allah expiates some of his sins thereby."

Harmalah ibn Yahya narrated to me: 'Abdullah ibn Wahb informed us: Haywah informed us: Ibn al-Had narrated to us, from Abu Bakr ibn Hazm, from 'Amrah, from 'A'ishah, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) say: "There is nothing that afflicts a believer, even a thorn that pricks him, but that Allah records for him a good deed thereby or erases from him a sin thereby."

Abu al-Tahir narrated to us: Ibn Wahb informed us: Malik ibn Anas informed me, from Yazid ibn Khusayfah, from 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, from 'A'ishah, the wife of the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "No affliction befalls a believer, even a thorn, but that some of his sins are deducted thereby or expiated thereby." Yazid did not know which of the two words 'Urwah said.

Abu al-Tahir narrated to me: Ibn Wahb informed us: Malik ibn Anas and Yunus ibn Yazid informed me, from Ibn Shihab, from 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, from 'A'ishah, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "There is no affliction that befalls a Muslim but that it is an expiation for him, even a thorn that pricks him."
Abu Kurayb narrated to us: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us: Hisham narrated to us, with this chain of transmission.

Muhammad ibn 'Abdillah ibn Numayr narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Bishr narrated to us: Hisham narrated to us, from his father, from 'A'ishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "No thorn pricks a believer, nor anything greater than it, but that Allah deducts from his sin thereby."
